justification: B keeps the Security callout with its installation code on B2, whereas A strands it at the top of A2, away from the step it warns about. B's numbered headings help a reader find their way through the procedures. A's opening is more compact, with the title band and content sharing A1, and its sans text is clean. B's centered cover page has a lot of empty space, and B3 leaves a large blank area. On balance, B's grouping and flow read better.

B orphans the balance-sheet Total row onto page B7 with only a repeated header, separated from its data. Design A keeps five account rows with the Total on A7. B also indents body text and tables in from the headings, which misaligns the left edge (B2, B4, B7). A's numbered headings and running header and footer bands give clearer navigation (A2, A4).

A uses bold section headings that clearly outrank the subheads. B's light-weight H1s ("1 Overview") are weaker than its bold H2s, which inverts the hierarchy. B splits Procedure 3 across a page break, leaving a lone step 1 on B4. Its heavy dark header and footer bands add clutter. A keeps each procedure intact on A5, though it leaves a nearly empty Troubleshooting page (A6) and has an inconsistent body size on A4.

B keeps the configuration table with its firmware section and packs the remaining sections onto four well-filled pages, whereas A orphans the parameter table onto page 4 away from its section and leaves page 5 mostly empty for a single small table. B's bold sans headings hung in the margin give clearer hierarchy and stronger structure. A has the more striking dark cover band.

A packs the content into 4 well-filled pages with a strong title band and consistent header/footer bands. B spreads it over 6 pages with a mostly empty cover (B1), a near-empty troubleshooting page (B6) and inconsistent body text sizing on B4. B also uses outdented headings that sit awkwardly at the margin. A's split of the security callout onto A2 is a minor flaw.

Both share layout and charts. A uses a sans heading/serif body pairing with larger, darker body text and numbered headings, giving clearer hierarchy and more legible running text. B's light, thin garamond body text at small size reads faint, and its section openers drop the large numerals. A's blue header/footer bands carry running heads and page counts, which aids navigation more than B's thin gold rule and small logo.

B's charts are taller with fuller axis ticks, so values read more easily than in A's squat charts (B4 and B7 vs A3 and A6). B pairs serif body text with sans headings and numbers its sections, which strengthens hierarchy (B5, B8). B also adds a contents page (B2). Otherwise the two designs share the same structure and bands. B's page 9 is not among the images shown, which keeps confidence at medium.

Both designs carry the same tables with repeated headers and shaded FY2026 columns. A orphans a single Q3 2025 Revenue row at the foot of A2, a split B avoids. That flaw is outweighed by A's strengths elsewhere. Its numbered section headings in a contrasting sans are bolder and easier to scan. Its running header and footer bands give section context on every page, e.g. 'Balance Sheet' and 'Page 4 of 7'. Its serif table text is crisper and more legible than B's light, small Garamond-style face. B's dark cover is striking, but its interior pages have only a thin top rule and a faint footer. B also splits the balance sheet with just two rows on B4.

A keeps each major section starting cleanly on its own page, with bold section headings and a serif body that reads well, though it leaves a near-empty cover and a sparse troubleshooting page. B is more compact and has a strong title band and running header/footer bands. However, its light-weight section headings (Overview, Configuration) are weaker than its bold subheadings, which inverts the hierarchy. B also separates the Security callout from its install step, and Procedure 3 splits mid-list across pages. A also has a minor inconsistency: the first procedure's closing note is set at a larger size than the others.

Same layouts throughout. A sets everything in a refined serif with a light gold rule and a small logo, which gives the pages a cohesive, editorial feel. B pairs a heavy sans for headings with a serif for body text. It also adds solid navy header and footer bars on every page, which feel heavier and more cluttered (B2–B7). B's section numbers on the dividers and in the running heads help navigation a little. A's 'Who rides' heading is weaker than its other section headings, but B has the same issue. Overall A reads as more polished.

A starts each major section on a fresh page and keeps procedures intact. Its serif text is refined, and its cover is clean. Its weaknesses are a mostly empty troubleshooting page (A6) and inconsistent body text size on A4. B is more compact and has stronger header and footer bands. However, it separates the Security callout from its install code (B1→B2) and splits Procedure 3 across pages (B3→B4), which hurts continuity for a procedural manual.

A uses numbered sans headings that stand out clearly from the serif body text, and its running headers give each page context. B's light, unnumbered serif headings stay elegant but are weaker for navigation. B's page 4 also has an inconsistent body size, with the 'Confirm the result' line set larger on B4. B's dark cover is attractive, but it ends with a nearly empty final page (B6) for the short troubleshooting section. A keeps its pacing tighter over 5 pages, though procedure 3 splits across A4 and A5.

B opens with a full-bleed illustrated cover and carries a consistent serif type system with gold rules and running headers. Its content flows continuously, so pages are evenly filled. A has a large empty lower half on A1 and an awkward hanging-indent body column offset from the headings. A also bleeds the illustration edge to edge mid-page on A3, leaving sparse pages. A's sans headings have punchier hierarchy, but B looks more polished and cohesive overall.

A pairs a serif body face with sans headings, which reads more comfortably than B's light grotesque body text. A also numbers its sections and divider pages ("2", "4") and includes a table of contents, giving clearer navigation (A2, A5, A8). A's charts are taller with finer axis ticks (A4, A7), while B's squashed charts lose detail (B3, B6). B does finish its document with an efficiency page (B8), whereas A's set ends at the divider. Both share the same weak spots: the 'Who rides' heading is set lighter than its own subhead (A7, B6), and pages are left with large empty lower halves.

A runs its content together compactly, with section rules, consistent indented text and a TOC. Its section heads hang outdented, which is slightly odd, but the pages are reasonably full. B spends two full pages on divider sidebars carrying only a short paragraph each (B4, B7). It leaves large empty bottoms on B3, B6 and B8. The 'Who rides' heading on B6 is set in a light weight, unlike the other bold heads. B's header and footer bands and blue charts look polished, but the fragmented pacing wastes space and weakens the hierarchy.

A pairs bold numbered sans headings with a serif body, so sections stand out clearly. B's light, unnumbered headings are weak, and its Appendix heading is smaller still, which muddles the hierarchy. B is more compact and avoids A's mostly empty final page. Even so, A's clearer typographic structure and separation of tables from the text that leads into them read better. A's table on A4 is cut off from its section, though.

B gives the report a full-bleed illustrated cover, so it opens more confidently. Its pull quote is set large as a real typographic moment, and its sections breathe evenly across pages. A's justified body text produces the hyphenation 're-placement' and loose word spacing on A2. A's running header also labels page 2 'Waste and packaging' when the page begins with the Climate content. B's charts use fuller axes, and B's serif body text reads more elegantly. The cover title in B sits over the building windows, which hurts legibility slightly, but overall B feels more polished.

A has a proper cover, a consistent green accent across charts and tables, and evenly filled pages. B's first page leaves its lower half empty under a short header band. Its hanging section headings sit misaligned with the indented body text. Its grey and black charts are flatter, and its full-bleed image on B3 breaks the margin rhythm.

Design A packs the content into three well-filled pages. Its colored title band leads straight into content. Its configuration table stays on the same page as its section (A2). Design B spends a near-empty cover page (B1). It splits the configuration table away from its section onto the Maintenance page (B4). It also leaves the appendix stranded on a mostly blank final page (B5). B's bolder, numbered headings are stronger than A's light headings, but A's overall pacing and page balance are better.

A keeps its total row with the last eight balance-sheet rows and the notes on A7. B strands the Total row alone under a repeated header on B7, which is a clear table break. B's headings also hang left of the indented body text, so the alignment is inconsistent. Its body text is letter-spaced and justified with loose gaps. A's serif set is more uniform, and its dark cover and top bands give a steady frame.

A packs the content into four well-filled pages and keeps the configuration table with its section on A3. B splits that table away from its section onto B4 and leaves B5 mostly empty with a single small appendix table. B's numbered headings and dark header and footer bands are tidy. Still, A's hanging indent and rule-led headings give a calmer, more consistent page rhythm. A's appendix sits as a subhead under Troubleshooting on A4, which is a minor hierarchy slip.

A pairs a refined serif with gold rules and gives the pull quote real presence (A2). Its ragged-right text avoids the stretched justified spacing and hyphenation seen in B (B2, B4). A's cover integrates the title over the illustration more elegantly (A1). B's cover is a blunt split, and B demotes the CEO quote to small italic. B does have clearer numbered headings and running headers (B2–B4).

B carries the green accent consistently through its charts and tables. It adds running headers and numbered sections, and it uses the illustration as a full cover. A has an odd left-hanging heading indent, which makes the alignment look inconsistent, and its charts are monochrome. However, A's sections each start a page with a clear pull-quote on A1, while B splits the Climate section across pages B2 and B3 and leaves a blank lower half on its cover. Overall B feels more cohesive and polished.

A strands the Total row alone on A7, separated from its table, while B keeps five rows above the Total on B7. A's bold Montserrat headings with indented body text are also slightly stronger than B's light numbered headings. B adds heavy dark header and footer bands that give running context, though they add visual weight. The orphaned total in A is the decisive flaw for a financial reader.

B keeps the security callout beside the install step it qualifies (B2). In A it is split onto the next page (A2). B also breaks sections more cleanly, with Configuration, Operations and Troubleshooting each starting a page. Its serif body text reads more calmly. A is more compact and has stronger header/footer bands, but its procedure list is cut mid-procedure across A3–A4 and the pages are crowded. B leaves a nearly empty final page (B6) and uses a full cover page, but it reads better overall.

B keeps the configuration-parameters table on the same page as the configuring section it belongs to (B3), whereas A pushes that table to the top of A4 under the Maintenance header. B also avoids A's near-empty final page (A5) by fitting the appendix onto B4. A's numbered headings and dark running bands give a solid structure, but B's ruled section breaks and hanging heads are just as clear. B's appendix is demoted to a smaller heading, which is a minor inconsistency.

The two designs carry nearly identical tables and pagination. A has a refined serif typeface, a strong dark cover and light running footers, so its table pages feel calm. B wraps every page in heavy dark header and footer bands. Its footer repeats the title, its body text is justified with gappy spacing (B2, B8), and its pages feel more cluttered. B's section numbering and running heads help navigation slightly, but overall A reads cleaner.

A uses bold sans headings that stand clearly apart from the serif body text. Its H1s hang out to the left of the indented body, which gives a strong hierarchy. B's light serif H1s (Overview, Configuration) are weaker than its own bold H3 procedure headings, so the hierarchy is inverted. B's dark cover and top rule bands are attractive, but the heading problem matters more to a reader. A's running headers repeat section names, though it has an odd font-size jump in the 'Confirm' line on A4, which B shares on B4.

Design B gives its charts more height and room, with fuller axes, on pages B4, B6 and B7. A's charts are squat on A3, A5 and A6, which leaves large empty lower halves on its pages. B also adds a table of contents (B2). A's heavy header and footer bands, sans type and running heads are tidy, but its charts feel cramped. B's serif type is elegant and readable throughout.

A uses a clean sans with tabular figures suited to dense financial tables, and running header and footer bands that name each section. The Balance Sheet starts on a fresh page in A4. B spends a whole page on a mostly empty dark cover (B1). It also opens the Balance Sheet with only two rows stranded at the bottom of B4. B's serif old-style numerals are less aligned for scanning columns, and its pages lack section labels in the running heads.

A pairs bold numbered sans headings with a serif body, so sections read clearly. B uses light, thin headings, and its 'Appendix' heading is barely larger than body text, which weakens the hierarchy. B's light-weight body text is also less readable. A has a proper cover with an illustration. Its charts are taller and its image is inset and framed. B squashes the charts and leaves its last pages two-thirds empty. B's green header bands are a nice touch, but they don't make up for the weak headings.

A strands the Total row alone on A7, cut off from its balance sheet with only a repeated header. B keeps the total attached to its final rows on B6. A's bare cover page is mostly empty, while B uses a compact title band and fills the pages more consistently. A has stronger serif-body typography and bolder section heads, but the orphaned total is the bigger flaw.

B packs the tables more densely, so it runs to 6 pages with no near-empty cover. Its running header and footer bands carry section names and page numbers, which aid navigation. A's serif type and dedicated cover look elegant, but A4 strands the balance-sheet heading after the long income table and the cover wastes a page. B's table splits are cleaner, giving a better rhythm across pages.

A uses bold, numbered sans headings that stand clearly above its serif body text. B's light serif headings sit close to body weight. B's "Appendix" heading is a small bold style that breaks from its other section heads (B4). B's cover title is cramped and overlaps the building windows, which hurts legibility (B1). A's cover sets the title on a clean green band (A1). B does stage the pull quote nicely, but its section hierarchy and cover are weaker overall.

A keeps the balance-sheet total with its last rows (A6), while B strands the Total row alone with a repeated header on the final page (B7). A also opens content right away under a strong header band. B spends a mostly empty cover page (B1), uses misaligned indented headings (B2, B4) and starts the balance sheet partway down a page (B4). A's consistent header and footer bands give a steadier rhythm.

A packs the content into three well-filled pages. Its compact title band leads straight into the content, and the configuration table stays with its section on A2. B spends a full page on a dark cover (B1). B3 is left half empty and the configuration table is pushed onto B4, away from its text. The appendix on B5 sits mostly alone on a blank page. B's serif type is elegant, but the pagination wastes space and breaks the flow.

B has numbered, bold sans headings that stand out from the serif body text. Its header and footer bands carry running section titles and 'Page x of 5', which help navigation. A uses light serif headings with orange rules and a strong dark cover, but its headings are weaker and its tiny footer is less useful. B's A5 appendix heading matches the other headings, while A's appendix heading is styled inconsistently from the rest.

A opens with a full illustrated cover and carries a consistent serif type system with gold rule accents and a coloured chart palette. Its pages are evenly filled. B crams the title band onto page one and leaves the lower half empty. B's hanging headings sit off the text column, its justified text shows loose spacing and hyphenation, and it uses plain grey charts. Its full-bleed image also breaks the margins.

A keeps each procedure intact; B splits Procedure 3 across pages B4–B5, orphaning step 1, and its heavy header and footer bands crowd the pages. A's text on A4 has an inconsistent body size, and A6 is mostly empty, but A's serif setting and section starts read more cleanly. B adds numbered headings and running heads, which helps navigation, but its title wraps awkwardly on B1.

A stays consistent and compact. Its sections flow continuously with uniform bold headings, and the charts and table pack tightly across A4–A6. B adds attractive navy header and footer bands and colour accents. However, its section treatment is inconsistent: sections 2 and 4 get full divider pages (B5, B8), while section 1 gets none and section 3 gets only a thin, light inline heading that is weaker than its own 3.1 subhead (B7). That disrupts both hierarchy and rhythm. B also leaves several pages mostly empty (B4, B6, B7).

A keeps numbered headings and a consistent body type size, and its header and footer bands frame each page well. B has one paragraph on B4 set noticeably larger than the rest of the text. B's outdented headings sit uneasily against the indented body. B also spills Troubleshooting onto a nearly empty sixth page. A's procedure split across pages is acceptable.

Design B packs the same content into three well-filled pages, with a compact header band and consistent running bands. Design A uses a full cover page and then leaves large empty lower halves on A2–A4. A5 is almost blank, holding only a short spec table, and its appendix heading style (bold) does not match the other section heads. A's serif text is pleasant and its cover is elegant, but B's pacing and balance are clearly better.

A has clearer, stronger section headings in bold, a more prominent pull quote, and a full-bleed image on A3. It also uses an indented serif body that is pleasant to read. However, A leaves large empty areas on A1 and A3, so the pages feel sparse and uneven. B flows content continuously across B1 to B3 with consistent left alignment. Its running header bands and green-tinted charts and tables tie in with the cover, and it uses space more evenly. B's light headings are weaker, but overall it reads as the more cohesive and balanced document.

A pairs a warm serif with a dedicated cover and a large pull quote, giving clearer hierarchy and a more considered editorial feel. B's sans text is set in a light grey weight with justified spacing gaps ('re-placement'). B also cramps the cover band onto content and shrinks the quote to a minor italic line, and its appendix heading is weak. Tables and charts are comparable in both.

Design A uses bold, numbered sans headings that stand out clearly from the serif body, and its running headers name the current section, which helps navigation in a manual. Design B's headings are light serif text that is barely heavier than the body. On B5 the appendix heading switches to a smaller bold style, which breaks the consistency. B's dark cover is striking, and its orange rules are elegant. A's teal bands are heavier, but they are consistent and useful.

A keeps one consistent sans family with green accents tying the charts and tables to the brand, and uses running header bands. Its pages are fuller, with three pages instead of four. B leaves page 1 half empty after the quote. It splits Climate from its chart, and its outdented headings against indented body text create awkward misalignment. B's oversized full-bleed illustration dominates page 3, and its grey-black charts drop the brand colour. B does have bolder section heads.

A keeps the security callout with its install code on A2. B splits it from the code, stranding it at the top of B2 under the Configuration context. A's numbered headings and serif body text give clearer hierarchy and easier long reading. B's banner cover is efficient, but its light-weight section heads and procedure titles lose numbering. A's cover page is mostly empty but conventional.

A pairs a refined serif with lighter running heads and includes a table of contents (A2). Its charts are taller and easier to read (A4, A6, A7). B's charts are squashed into very short strips with sparse axes (B3, B6, B9), and its heavy navy header and footer bands crowd every page. B does include the final efficiency page that A appears to lack, but overall A reads as more polished.

B pairs a bold sans heading face with a serif text face. Its headings are clearly heavier than its body text, while A's light headings sit close to its body weight, as on A1 and A3. B's hanging indent gives a clear structure, and its clean title page and generous margins read more refined. A's banded header and footer are cohesive, but its light headings weaken the hierarchy.

A packs the content into four well-filled pages. On A3 the configuration table stays with its section, and the appendix sits on A4. B moves the parameters table to B4, away from its section on B3, which leaves B3 half empty. B also gives the short appendix its own mostly blank page (B5). B's dark cover and orange bands look polished. Even so, A's bold sans headings give clearer hierarchy and its pacing is tighter.

A applies a consistent navy-and-gold palette, a header rule, and divider pages with a section-number tab band (A5, A8), which give clear structure. Its weaknesses are large empty lower halves (A3, A4, A7) and an inconsistent "Who rides" heading in a lighter weight (A7). B packs content densely but continuously (B4–B6). It uses hanging section heads that break the margin and justified text with uneven spacing, and its dark, plain palette is less distinctive. A feels more designed and easier to navigate.

Design A strands the balance sheet Total row alone on A7, separated from its table by a repeated header. Design B keeps the total with the last eight accounts on B7, which reads far better. A's bold sans headings give stronger hierarchy and its white cover is crisp. B's dark cover and consistent top rule look more polished. A also splits quarters awkwardly across pages (Q3 2025 at the bottom of A2).

B is more compact and consistent. Its teal title band, header and footer bands and orange section rules give a clear, unified identity across three pages. A spends a whole sparse page on the title and hangs its headings out to the left of the indented body text. B's light-weight headings are slightly weaker, and A's bold headings and serif body have more contrast, but B reads more cohesively overall.

B's banner cover gets straight into the income statement and the document runs to 6 pages. Its income statement ends cleanly on B3, so the Balance Sheet starts at the top of B4. In A, the income table spills onto A4 and the balance sheet begins squeezed below it, and the mostly empty cover page A1 adds bulk. A's serif type and centred cover are elegant, but B's section breaks are cleaner. Both designs end on a sparse Notes page.

B uses bold numbered section headings that stand out clearly from the serif body text. A's light-weight headings are weak, and its 'Appendix' heading is even smaller than the others (A3). B's cover gives the illustration a deliberate full-bleed role. Its charts are taller and easier to read. The waste illustration is framed with margins instead of A's cropped full-width strip (A2 vs B3). A's 3 pages are denser, but A1 crams the title band, KPIs and chart together, while B's pacing is calmer.

A has consistent navy branding, header and footer bands, and divider pages with a progress sidebar. But many of its pages are mostly empty, with small charts floating at the top (A3, A5, A6, A8). Its 'Who rides' heading on A6 is inconsistent, a light weight unlike the other section titles. B flows the content continuously with larger, more legible charts (B4, B5, B6) and adds a contents page (B2). It wastes less space and reads more cohesively, though its serif body text and justified spacing are slightly uneven.

A has a consistent navy palette, numbered sections, running header and footer bands, and divider pages with a side navigation tab. The result is a clear and branded structure. Its weak spots are section 3, which loses its divider page and uses a light heading (A7), and many half-empty pages. B is more compact. However, its monochrome black charts are duller, section headings hang outside the text margin (B4, B5), and sections run together without much separation. It is also cut off after page 6. Overall A reads as the more finished report.

A puts its title band directly above the content, so no page is wasted. The Balance Sheet begins on its own page (A4), which keeps the sections cleanly separated. B spends a full mostly-empty cover page (B1). B4 starts the Balance Sheet in a cramped tail of a page after the income table, leaving only five rows before the break. B's serif table text is a bit denser and less crisp for figures than A's clean sans with tabular alignment. Both end with a sparse notes page.

B's bold sans headings make clearer contrast against body text and give the sections stronger hierarchy (B2–B4). A's light serif section heads are weak beside its bold subheads (A2, A4). A has a stronger dark cover and top bands (A1), but B's running headers with section names help navigation. B's hanging headings that break left of the text block look slightly odd, though. Both share the same issues: the clipped 'Worker' label in the diagram and mostly empty troubleshooting pages.

B adds polished gold header bands and section divider pages, but it applies them unevenly. Reliability and Costs and carbon get full divider pages (B5, B8), while Who rides gets only a small plain heading (B7). B also ends on the Costs and carbon divider (B8); the efficiency charts and closing text that A shows on A6 never appear. Several B pages are left mostly empty (B4, B6). A runs consistently and keeps every section, with steady chart-and-text flow on A4–A6.
